q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of glass wool insulation?
title: Glass wool insulation carbon footprint per kg
short: Add the glass batch and cullet, the binder and the facing per kg of insulation using supplier figures. Add melting, fiberising, curing and packing energy, then divide the plant's energy by kg made.

ul: Sand, soda ash, borax and recycled glass cullet.
Foil or kraft facing if used.
Melting, often electric or gas fired.

p: Report per kg, or per square metre by thickness and density. Melting is often the largest energy line.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 224,000 / 500,000 = 0.448 kg CO2 per kg
Add batch materials and binder for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
